source: U.S. Bureau of Labor Statistics, Public Data API v2 (no registration key)
series_description: Consumer Price Index for All Urban Consumers (CPI-U), U.S. city average, All items, Not Seasonally Adjusted, 1982-84=100
license: U.S. government work -- public domain, no restriction on reuse
fetch_method: Three live HTTPS GET requests to api.bls.gov (startyear/endyear windows 2006-2015, 2016-2025, 2026-2026 -- the public, unregistered API caps each request at a 10-year span), merged and deduplicated by calendar month.

real_data_gap.2025-10: BLS did not publish this month's index value, citing the 2025 lapse in appropriations (a real government shutdown) -- left absent in the CSV rather than interpolated or forward-filled. This also makes 2026-10's year-over-year change uncomputable (needs the 2025-10 base) and is left blank for the same honest reason.

transformation: CPI_YOY is (level[t] / level[t-12] - 1) * 100, computed only where both the current and 12-months-prior level exist.

publication_lag_assumption_days.note: A FIXED, documented assumption (BLS's own well-publicized release schedule: the CPI for month M is released in a press release roughly 2 weeks into month M+1), not fetched real per-release vintage data (ALFRED, which has true vintage timestamps, is unreachable from this environment -- see CHECKLIST_STATUS.md's DAT-02/DAT-03 entries). Each month's CPI_YOY value is treated as first knowable 15 days after that month's own month-end, i.e. effectively mid-month M+1.

sanity_checks.2008-12: 0.09% YoY -- the real, well-documented disinflation collapse during the 2008 financial crisis (from 5.6% in 5 months earlier)
sanity_checks.2020-05: 0.12% YoY -- the real COVID-19 demand-shock disinflation trough
sanity_checks.2022-06: 9.06% YoY -- the real 2022 US inflation surge peak (BLS's own widely-reported headline figure for this month was 9.1% on the seasonally-adjusted series; this NSA series' 9.06% is the expected, very close NSA/SA difference, not a data error)
